name: Marc Ramos
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I taught myself to skate braking against our sofa.” Monday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Marc keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I delivered the missing keys on my skates. It's the first time a grown-up thanked me for using the pavement.
appearance: Marc has auburn hair cut square at the nape, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Marc starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Marc has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Marc knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To be trusted with another small delivery on skates.
family: Nessa Wren is Marc’s parent’s cousin. Marc brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Nessa makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Window seven*, Nessa says, “I promised her we'd try. I kept saying try because of the time I promised my father a trip he never got to make.”
connections: Billie Morrow. The soup tin has to travel another route with a rider who now knows where it belongs.

reactions.situation: A tenant refuses to hand back a spare key
reactions.response: Marc asks the tenant what access they would be giving up.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Marc keeps the customer's place while they check the amount and gets the impatient people talking about something else.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Marc asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
